Bright Memory is a short FPS with surprisingly satisfying combat. The shooting feels great, and the fast-paced gameplay is a lot of fun. The dodge mechanic is a cool addition, although accidentally triggering it by double-tapping a movement key can get annoying.

The story is probably my biggest issue. There isn’t much context or explanation, so it can be pretty confusing. Hopefully, Bright Memory: Infinite expands on the story and gives more context.

The graphics are also quite impressive, especially for such a short game.

Overall, I enjoyed my time with it.

Frankly one of the most enjoyable experiences I've had in a while. It's a massive upgrade from it's first game, and it has a very enjoyable story (it's a bit flawed and full of holes you can poke on but it ended up being really a fun thing to talk about).

Kickass gameplay and soundtrack, I hope Sega considers making a third game soon!

With the announcement on social media from CEO Thomas Mahler that No Rest for the Wicked, and this is a direct quote, is "using AI to help with tooling, bugfixes and so on, like everyone else is. We'd be stupid not to. It's a genuinely useful tool."

I'm going to be giving this game a "Do Not Recommend."

The use of generative ai in any part of production is wholesale just cutting out work from real humans. The fact of saying "we aren't using it for art assets" does not mean you aren't using it in your pipeline.

You've used it in your pipeline and thus should have had to disclose this on your Steam page.

The first Planet of Lana game was wonderful in many ways but the gameplay was a bit shallow. This sequel is a continuation of the narrative with more and more diverse gameplay and a stunning step up for the animation, backdrops, and sound. Some scenes are truly breathtaking.

It's delightful to move through this world and dive deeper into the story. There are new puzzle-solving mechanics and characters to meet. Still, the gameplay is not the strongest element. Though there are some good puzzles, many are mundane. It does, however, play well enough to keep things interestingly interactive as the story and presentation take center stage.

I can't wait for the next game in the series!

A very entertaining metroidvania adventure comparable to a smaller-scale Hollow Knight. The art and music style is appealing and I always enjoy pixel-art. The worldbuilding is solid. Without spoilers, the plot is intriguing and the sparse NPCs really sells that you're treading through a dying land. Combat takes after Hollow Knight, little guy with a big sword, but unlike Hollow Knight there are no ranged abilities you can use. The healing mechanic is unique but is trivial lategame. 

The biggest flaw of the game from what I have heard and experienced  is the bosses. They are quite damage spongey, and if you're on your first playthrough they will pummel you into the dirt. With the knowledge of a first playthrough however, I found the bosses to be significantly easier. 

If you like the metroidvania genre, then I strongly recommend buying Haiku the Robot.

Huge W to the Thompson brothers! 

After hearing all praise surrounding their newest title, "Well Dweller", I decided to take a look into their catologue of games and play through all of them from oldest to newest. Sheepo was the first game of theirs I had completed and really gave me a tatse for the quality of the games they create. As of writing this review I have just 100% completed "Islets", and can't wait to continue with "Crypt Custodian!" Obviously this game does have sertain flaws to it especially when comparing it to Kyle and Eric's newer titles, but for their first game I was left very impressed with the creativity behind this title. Fun and sometimes challenging platforming, really viby music to accompany this game's soundtrack, and a super cute and gorgeous artstyle are all factors that have made me come to love Sheepo as a game. For sure would reccomend! ;)

Besides the fact this game has no one playing it. My friend and I bought the game. We had a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blast. The bots do try to murder you if they are the killer. They do collect resources and hoard them sometimes. This game is fun to play with friends. A dead game is only dead until people revive it. Does it need some optimization? Yeah, a bit, there is a delay in when the game announces someone dies. A mic bug that's solved by leaving the lobby and coming back. Those are my biggest issues. However, I love the look of it cause it's like those old PS2 games honestly. I've seen worse graphics. This game is fun and we bought it on a sale. Major props to the Dev who kept putting out content and bug fixes when the game slowed down. Even put out a Halloween event. I hope it comes out this year too, cause I would like to play it with my friends.
